Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a chat application written in Rust (a port of the Rails app, compatible with its database). Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Let's add a new feature—bots. Bots can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.

Any chat member can create and manage bots via the user interface:
- open the account settings page (`/account/edit`)
- click the bot icon ("Set up chat bots")

This opens the bots page (`/bots`). It lists the bots you created (administrators see all bots) and has the "Add a chat bot" button. The button opens the `/bots/new` page with a form:

- bot avatar (optional)
- bot name (required), labelled "Name the bot"
- the "Save changes" button

Submitting the form creates a bot and redirects back to `/bots`. Each bot on the list shows its name and its unique bot code in a read-only field labelled "Bot code", in the same list item—the code is used to authenticate bot requests. The bot code is a sensitive credential. The bots page shows all of your bots on one page, without pagination.

From the list, you can also edit a bot (name, avatar): each bot has an "Edit <bot name>" link (for example, "Edit Deploy Bot") to its edit page. The edit page uses the same form and has a "Delete this chat bot" button that asks for confirmation. A deleted bot can no longer post messages.

Like any new user, a new bot joins all open rooms. Bots can be added to other rooms the same way as people.

Here is how a bot can post a message:

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Bots can post from shell scripts and CI jobs. The raw request body becomes the message body. No JSON envelope, no field names.

The endpoint responds with:

- `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`
- `422 Unprocessable Content` — empty body and no attachment
- `404 Not Found` — bad room id
- `401 Unauthorized` — invalid bot code

The message is broadcast to connected clients and triggers push notifications exactly as a human-authored message would.

The message shows the bot (its name) as the author.

  "output": "# once-campfire-rust

Campfire, the chat app, in Rust. It runs existing Rails Campfire installs
([basecamp/once-campfire](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire)) without migrating data.

- Stay compatible with existing installs unless told otherwise: the SQLite schema, the storage
  layout, and signed/encrypted cookies (so people stay signed in across an upgrade).
- List behavior that differs from Rails Campfire under "Known differences" in `README.md`.

## Layout

| Path | Package | What |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/` | — | `dev`: local server and seed |
| `crates/ruby` | `ruby_compat` | Ruby's own string behaviour the other crates share (ERB escaping, `String#to_i`/`#to_f`/`#strip`, `Float#to_s`, `CGI.escape`, `ERB::Util.url_encode`, Active Record's integer binding, Rack's byte ranges), checked by `vectors/ruby_core.json`; no dependencies |
| `crates/rails_compat` | `rails_compat` | Rails signing/encryption/serialization contracts and the Rails formats several crates write (`ActiveSupport::JSON`, `Content-Disposition`), checked by `vectors/`, and the app's `Clock` (`Time.current`, and time travel for tests) |
| `crates/kit` | `campfire_kit` | Axum adapter, `Ctx`, params, cookies, session, forgery protection, flash, formats, responses, gzip, and the front server (TLS, ACME, HTTP/2, response cache) |
| `crates/routes` | `campfire_routes` | Path helpers for the app's routes |
| `crates/db` | `campfire_db` | rusqlite over the schema, models, queries, fixtures (`fixtures/`) and their loader |
| `crates/richtext` | `campfire_richtext` | Rich text content pipeline: sanitize, attachments, autolink, plain text |
| `crates/storage` | `campfire_storage` | Active Storage-compatible blobs, disk service, variants (libvips), previews (ffmpeg) |
| `crates/cable` | `campfire_cable` | Action Cable protocol server, its WebSocket implementation, and in-process pub/sub |
| `crates/assets` | `campfire_assets` | The frontend (`app/`, `vendor/`, `public/`, `importmap.rb`), digested and embedded at build time |
| `crates/views` | `campfire_views` | Askama templates and view helpers |
| `crates/campfire` | `campfire` (bin) | Controllers, router wiring, channels, jobs, integrations, seeds |
| `vectors/` | — | Frozen test data (recorded from Rails and Ruby) and `test.env`, the fixed test-only keys |
| `bench/` | — | Load generator, benchmark scripts and recorded results |

## Working rules

- Rust comes from mise if it isn't on the PATH: `mise exec rust@1.98.1 -- cargo ...` (the version
  in `Dockerfile`).
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude html5ever` runs everything. The app's integration tests build
  their seed databases themselves.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude html5ever --all-targets` should stay clean. (`html5ever` is a
  vendored copy with one backported fix and two small additions for Gumbo's parse limits, all
  recorded in its `Cargo.toml`, and identical to upstream otherwise.)
- Format with `cargo fmt --all` (`rustfmt.toml`) before committing, and `bench/loadgen`, a workspace
  of its own, with `cargo fmt --manifest-path bench/loadgen/Cargo.toml`; CI checks both. The
  vendored html5ever has its own `rustfmt.toml` that turns formatting off, and generated tables are
  marked `#[rustfmt::skip]`.
- CI also runs `cargo shear` for dependencies declared but not used. When it can't see a real use
  (a build script's `#[path]` modules, a self dev-dependency), list the crate under
  `[package.metadata.cargo-shear] ignored` in that manifest, with the reason.
- Put shared dependency versions in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`, and reference them with
  `foo.workspace = true`.
- Frontend changes go in `crates/assets/app/`. `crates/assets/vendor/` holds third-party
  JavaScript and CSS, copied byte-for-byte (see its `MANIFEST.md`); don't edit it.
- Write code that reads like the surrounding code: small, clearly named functions, and comments
  only where the behavior is non-obvious. Say why when behavior deliberately differs from Rails
  Campfire.
- Tests live beside the code. Golden-vector tests read `vectors/*.json`.
- Performance changes come with before-and-after measurements, recorded under `bench/results/`.
"

# Bots Feature

## Overview
Bots in Campfire can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.
Each bot is backed by a User record (which allows seamless integration with memberships, avatar rendering, message authorship, and broadcasts) and a Bot record containing the sensitive authentication `bot_code`.

## User Interface
- Account settings page (`/account/edit`): contains a "Set up chat bots" link with the bot icon in the navigation bar.
- Bots index (`/bots`):
  - Displays all bots created by the current user (administrators see all bots).
  - Listed on a single page without pagination.
  - Displays each bot's avatar, name, unique bot code in a read-only input labelled "Bot code", and an "Edit <bot name>" link.
  - Includes an "Add a chat bot" button linking to `/bots/new`.
- New bot page (`/bots/new`):
  - Form with optional avatar upload, required bot name labelled "Name the bot", and a "Save changes" submit button.
  - Creating a bot grants membership to all open rooms (`RoomType::Open`) via User creation hooks.
  - Redirects to `/bots`.
- Edit bot page (`/bots/:id/edit`):
  - Uses the same form (avatar and bot name labelled "Name the bot", "Save changes" button).
  - Features a "Delete this chat bot" button asking for browser-native confirmation (`data-turbo-confirm` and `confirm()`).
  - Deleting a bot removes its entry from `bots` and deactivates its User record, revoking posting access.

## HTTP API
```
POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages
```
Raw body becomes the message text without JSON wrapping or form field names.

Responses:
- `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`
- `422 Unprocessable Content` if body is empty / whitespace
- `404 Not Found` if room does not exist or bot is not a member of the room
- `401 Unauthorized` if bot code is invalid or bot was deleted

The message is broadcast over ActionCable to connected clients and push notifications are queued for room members.
EOF

steps.message:
I have implemented the bots feature for Campfire following all specifications and conventions:

1. **Database Schema & Model**:
   - Added `bots` table and indexes (`index_bots_on_code`, `index_bots_on_user_id`, `index_bots_on_creator_id`) to database additions.
   - Implemented `Bot` model in `crates/db/src/models/bot.rs` supporting creation, deletion, lookup by code, user ID, creator ID, and code generation.

2. **Routes & Routing**:
   - Added path helpers in `crates/routes/src/lib.rs` for `bots`, `new_bot`, `bot(id)`, `edit_bot(id)`, and `bot_messages(room_id, bot_code)`.
   - Wired the controller routes in `crates/campfire/src/controllers.rs`.
   - Allowed raw request bodies in `crates/kit/src/adapter.rs` without form urlencoded parse errors on the bot messaging route.

3. **Views & User Interface**:
   - Added the bot icon link with label "Set up chat bots" to `/account/edit`.
   - Implemented `bots/index.html` listing bots on a single page without pagination, showing each bot's name, read-only field labelled "Bot code" in the same list item, "Add a chat bot" button, and "Edit <bot name>" link.
   - Implemented `bots/new.html` with optional avatar upload, bot name input labelled "Name the bot", and "Save changes" submit button.
   - Implemented `bots/edit.html` with the same form plus a "Delete this chat bot" button using native browser `confirm()`.

4. **Controllers & Bot Message API**:
   - Implemented `BotsController` handling CRUD actions and permissions (non-admins see and edit only their own bots, admins see all).
   - Creating a bot creates an underlying user record, automatically granting membership to all open rooms.
   - Implemented `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` accepting raw request body text:
     - Returns `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`.
     - Returns `422 Unprocessable Content` on empty/whitespace body.
     - Returns `404 Not Found` for invalid room IDs or rooms where the bot is not a member.
     - Returns `401 Unauthorized` for invalid or deleted bot codes.
     - Broadcasts messages to ActionCable subscribers and queues push notifications with the bot as author.

5. **Testing & Documentation**:
   - Created comprehensive tests covering bot models, CRUD workflows, permissions, and API responses.
   - Added design notes to `docs/bots.md`.
   - All workspace tests compile cleanly and pass.
